reason: The hypothesis combines the known formation of a protective Cr2O3 layer on FeNiCrCoCu (P1, P3) with the general concept of an optimal oxide thickness for wear resistance (P12, P17, P23) and applies it specifically to a controlled pre-oxidation intervention on a thin-film coating. However, the core idea—that a pre-formed, optimally thin Cr2O3 layer mediates high-temperature wear resistance—is a direct restatement of findings and mechanisms already reported in P1 and P3, which show that thermal exposure forms a protective Cr2O3 layer that enhances wear resistance.
